title: kill-broker SIGTERMs every peer's MCP server, not just the broker
description:
## Symptom

Running `bun cli.ts kill-broker` SIGTERMs every MCP server connected to the broker (claude-peers and opencode-peers child processes), not just the listening broker daemon. Observed live on 2026-05-06: a single `kill-broker` call killed 6 peer MCP servers and even self-terminated the cli.ts process (exit 143).

## Root cause

In `cli.ts` the `kill-broker` case shells out to:

    lsof -ti :PORT

That returns **every** pid with an open socket on the port — both the listener and every connected client. Each peer's MCP server holds a long-lived TCP connection for `/poll-messages` (every ~1s), so they all show up in the list. The loop then `process.kill(pid, "SIGTERM")` over the whole set, including the cli.ts process itself if its `brokerFetch("/health")` socket is still in lsof's snapshot.

## Fix

Filter lsof to listening sockets only:

    lsof -t -iTCP:PORT -sTCP:LISTEN

This returns only the broker process. Should be a one-line change in the `kill-broker` case in `cli.ts` (around line 384).

## Acceptance criteria

- `bun cli.ts kill-broker` only kills the broker process. Connected MCP servers (claude-peers, opencode-peers) survive.
- Manual repro: start the broker, register 2+ peers via the runtimes, run kill-broker, then verify the peer MCP servers are still alive (e.g., pgrep -f runtimes/claude/server.ts still returns).
- The cli.ts process itself does not self-terminate (no exit 143).

## Notes

While we're in there, consider: if no broker is found via the LISTEN filter, print "broker not running" instead of silently doing nothing. Currently the catch swallows that case.
close_reason: Fixed in 25c8d88. lsof now filtered to LISTEN-state sockets only. Verified empirically on live broker (pid 58299): old query returned 6 pids (broker + 5 opencode peers), fixed query returns 1 (just the broker). Regression covered by tests/cli-kill-broker.test.ts (2 tests passing).

title: Wrap-up: human verification across terminals + open PR
description:
Final task in the terminal-title-summary branch. Runs the full human-verification checklist across multiple terminals, then opens the PR.

This task does NOT add new functionality — it's the gating step that confirms everything works end-to-end on real terminal emulators (which automated tests can't cover) and ships the work.

PRECONDITIONS
- All of upm-7e8, upm-nt2, upm-cnt, upm-3sz, upm-74z closed.
- Branch terminal-title-summary up to date with main (rebase if needed).
- bun test passes locally.

HUMAN VERIFICATION CHECKLIST (run each, check off in PR description)

Ghostty:
[ ] Fresh claude-code session in a Ghostty window. Title becomes [<id>] <auto-summary> within ~1s of launch.
[ ] Ask agent to set_summary 'short test'. Title updates immediately.
[ ] Ask agent to set_summary with a long string (>120 chars). Title truncates cleanly.
[ ] Ask agent to set_summary with a multi-line string containing escape codes. Title shows sanitized single-line text; no garbled rendering.
[ ] Ctrl+C the session. Title clears (next shell prompt reclaims).
[ ] kill -9 the MCP server process. Title is allowed to remain stale (clear-title is graceful-shutdown only) — confirm this is what happens, not a crash.

iTerm or Terminal.app (verifies generic adapter):
[ ] Same flow as Ghostty, baseline behavior. Title updates correctly via generic OSC 2.

tmux (verifies multiplexer pass-through):
[ ] Inside a tmux session with set-titles on, fresh claude-code. Outer terminal title reflects [<id>] <summary>. Document if it doesn't (likely a tmux config note for the README rather than a code fix).

Multi-peer:
[ ] Two claude-code sessions in separate Ghostty windows. Each window's title shows its OWN peer ID, not the other's.
[ ] One claude-code + one opencode peer. Both titles update correctly (adapter selection driven by terminal_program, not runtime).

CLI:
[ ] bun cli.ts peers prints peer info including terminal_program.
[ ] bun cli.ts retitle <id> re-asserts that peer's title.

PR
- Open PR against main. Body includes the checklist above with checkmarks, screenshots/screen-recording of at least the Ghostty case, and a note about the upm-azr deferred follow-up.
- Squash-merge or fast-forward per repo convention (no convention enforced; pick what matches recent merges).
notes:
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT (per user 2026-05-07): every PR must ship with README.md / docs updates covering the user-visible changes.

Final-PR doc checklist (verify before opening PR):
[ ] README.md has a 'Terminal title' section explaining: titles auto-update from peer summaries via OSC 2 to /dev/<tty>, the format ([id] summary), the adapter pattern's role, how to verify, behavior in tmux/unknown terminals.
[ ] README.md HTTP endpoints table includes /clear-title and /retitle (added in upm-3sz / upm-74z).
[ ] README.md CLI section includes 'bun cli.ts retitle <id>' (added in upm-74z).
[ ] README.md Environment table includes UPM_TTY_DIR (added in upm-cnt as a test seam, but worth documenting since it's user-overridable for sandboxed setups).
[ ] If a CHANGELOG.md or similar exists, add an entry. (Currently doesn't exist; skip.)
[ ] AGENTS.md — check if it needs updates (it didn't reference set_summary's side effects before).

title: Add /retitle broker endpoint + cli.ts retitle subcommand
description:
Diagnostic / recovery path for re-asserting a peer's title after it's been clobbered (e.g. by a long ssh session that set its own title, by tmux disabling set-titles, etc.).

Changes:
- shared/types.ts: add RetitleRequest = { id: PeerId }.
- broker.ts: new POST /retitle endpoint. Handler looks up the peer and re-runs getAdapter(peer.terminal_program).writeTitle(peer.tty, formatTitle(peer)) — same logic as the in-line call from handleSetSummary, just on demand.
- cli.ts: add 'retitle <peer-id>' subcommand that hits POST /retitle. Mirror the style of existing send / peers / etc. subcommands.

Verify: bun cli.ts peers to find a live peer ID, then bun cli.ts retitle <id> — that peer's terminal title is re-asserted. Useful for debugging adapter wiring and for the user to recover from a clobbered title without restarting the agent.
notes:
TESTS to add (reuses fakeTty + spawnBroker helpers from upm-cnt):
- broker.test.ts:
    * Test: register peer with fake TTY. Drain bytes. POST /retitle. Assert fresh OSC 2 with current [<id>] <summary> received.
    * Test: POST /retitle with unknown peer ID — returns 404.
- cli.test.ts (new):
    * Spawn cli.ts retitle <id> as a subprocess against the spawnBroker helper. Assert exit code 0 and that the fake TTY received the OSC 2.
    * Spawn cli.ts retitle <bogus-id>. Assert non-zero exit code and a clear error message on stderr.

HUMAN VERIFICATION
- bun cli.ts peers — confirm output shows live peer IDs and their terminal_program field.
- Note a peer's title in Ghostty. From a different shell: bun cli.ts retitle <id>. Title is re-asserted (visible briefly if it had been clobbered).
- Run bun cli.ts retitle <bogus-id>. Confirm clean error message, no broker crash.

title: Add /clear-title endpoint and claude runtime exit cleanup
description:
When a peer shuts down cleanly, restore the terminal title so the user isn't left looking at a stale agent summary.

Changes:
- shared/types.ts: add ClearTitleRequest = { id: PeerId }.
- broker.ts: new POST /clear-title endpoint (route alongside other endpoints around lines 380-395). Handler looks up the peer, calls getAdapter(peer.terminal_program).clearTitle(peer.tty). Fire-and-forget.
- runtimes/claude/server.ts: in the existing SIGINT/exit path (search around the polling loop / shutdown logic), call brokerFetch('/clear-title', { id: myId }) on graceful shutdown. Best-effort — wrap in try/catch and ignore failures so it doesn't block exit.

Verify: start a claude-code session, watch the Ghostty title update on register. Quit cleanly with Ctrl+D or :q-equivalent. Confirm title clears (next shell prompt reclaims it as expected). Hard-kill the process (kill -9) — title may stay stale, that's acceptable since this is the graceful-shutdown path.
notes:
TESTS to add (reuses fakeTty + spawnBroker helpers from upm-cnt):
- broker.test.ts:
    * Test: register peer with fake TTY. POST /clear-title. Assert fakeTty.getBytes() contains '\x1b]2;\x07' (empty title OSC).
    * Test: POST /clear-title with unknown peer ID — returns 404, no crash.

For the SIGINT path in runtimes/claude/server.ts, add a runtimes/claude/server.test.ts that:
    * Imports the cleanup function (extract it as an exported function for testability).
    * Spy / mock brokerFetch and assert /clear-title is called with the right body when cleanup runs.
    * Confirms cleanup swallows fetch errors silently (best-effort).

HUMAN VERIFICATION
- Ghostty session with claude-code. Note the title.
- Cleanly quit (Ctrl+C in claude-code, or :q-equivalent for opencode). Title clears within 1s; the next shell prompt sets its own title naturally.
- Restart claude-code in same window. Title sets to new peer's [<id>] <summary> — confirms no leftover state.
- Hard-kill the MCP server (kill -9). Title remains stale (this is acceptable / documented). Confirm broker still works for other peers and didn't crash.

title: Wire title write into register + set_summary handlers
description:
Make the terminal title actually reflect the peer summary by hooking the adapter into the broker's two state-change paths.

Changes in broker.ts:
- handleRegister (lines 148-180): after the insert succeeds, call getAdapter(peer.terminal_program).writeTitle(peer.tty, formatTitle(peer)). Fire-and-forget — don't block registration on the write.
- handleSetSummary (lines 197-199): after updateSummary.run, look up the peer with getPeer.get(body.id), then call the same adapter.writeTitle. Fire-and-forget.

Both call sites use the formatTitle helper from shared/terminals/format.ts to produce '[<peer-id>] <summary>'.

Verify:
1. Start a fresh claude-code session in Ghostty. Confirm window title becomes '[<id>] <auto-summary>' shortly after launch.
2. Have the agent call set_summary with a new string. Title updates within ~1s.
3. Repeat in iTerm or Terminal.app — confirm generic adapter handles it (TERM_PROGRAM unknown to registry).
4. Start an opencode peer — title also updates (adapter selection driven by terminal_program, not runtime).
notes:
TESTS to add (this is where the integration harness lives — reused by upm-3sz and upm-74z):
- broker.test.ts:
    * Helper: createFakeTty() — creates a temp file path (e.g. /tmp/upm-test-tty-<pid>-<rand>) and starts a background reader that buffers all bytes written to it. Returns { path, getBytes(), close() }.
    * Helper: spawnBroker() — picks a free port, sets PEERS_PORT env, spawns broker as a child process, awaits ready. Returns { port, close() }.
    * Test: register a peer with tty = fakeTty.path. Verify fakeTty.getBytes() contains '\x1b]2;[<id>] ' soon after register.
    * Test: POST /set-summary with a new summary. Verify the fake TTY received a fresh OSC 2 with the new summary.
    * Test: POST /set-summary with control-byte-laden summary — verify bytes received are sanitized (no control bytes other than the framing ESC and BEL).

These helpers are exported from broker.test.ts utils so upm-3sz and upm-74z reuse them.

HUMAN VERIFICATION
- Live Ghostty window. Start claude-code. Title becomes [<id>] <auto-summary> within ~1s.
- Ask agent: 'call set_summary with the text working on adapter pattern'. Title updates immediately to [<id>] working on adapter pattern.
- Ask agent: 'call set_summary with a 200-character lorem ipsum'. Title truncates cleanly, no rendering glitches.
- Open a second Ghostty window with claude-code. Confirm each window has its own peer ID in its title — no cross-talk.
close_reason: title write wired into register + set_summary; integration harness shared via tests/harness.ts; README + CLAUDE.md updated

title: Add terminal_program field to Peer schema, types, and registration
description:
Persist which terminal emulator hosts each peer so the broker can pick the right adapter per peer.

Changes:
- broker.ts: add 'terminal_program TEXT' column to peers table schema (around lines 53-66). Add startup migration: PRAGMA table_info(peers) → if column missing, ALTER TABLE peers ADD COLUMN terminal_program TEXT. Update insert prepared statement to include it.
- shared/types.ts: add 'terminal_program: string | null' to Peer interface; add 'terminal_program?: string' to RegisterRequest.
- runtimes/claude/server.ts: at registration (around lines 437-446), read process.env.TERM_PROGRAM and pass it through in the RegisterRequest body. (Ghostty sets TERM_PROGRAM=Ghostty, iTerm sets iTerm.app, Terminal.app sets Apple_Terminal.)
- broker.ts handleRegister (lines 148-180): accept and persist terminal_program. (No title write here yet — that's the next task.)

Verify: start a fresh peer, query the DB, confirm terminal_program is populated with the expected value (e.g. Ghostty). Existing peers without the column should still work after migration.
notes:
(Augments existing conventions notes)

title: Add terminal adapter scaffolding (shared/terminals/)
description:
Lay down the adapter infrastructure for terminal interactions so future per-terminal features (badges, flash, AppleScript window targeting) plug in cleanly without touching broker logic.

Files to create:
- shared/terminals/types.ts — TerminalAdapter interface (name, writeTitle, clearTitle). All methods are no-throw / silent-fail.
- shared/terminals/generic.ts — Generic OSC 2 adapter. Standard \033]2;<title>\007 to /dev/<tty>. Sanitizes input (strips control bytes), no-ops on null tty, catches write errors silently.
- shared/terminals/ghostty.ts — Ghostty adapter. Initially identical to generic; exists as the seam for Ghostty-specific features (OSC 9 notifications, AppleScript, future flash tool from upm-azr).
- shared/terminals/format.ts — formatTitle(peer: Peer): string producing '[<id>] <summary>'. Sanitizes summary, truncates to 120 chars total. Falls back to '[<id>] <runtime>' if summary is empty.
- shared/terminals/index.ts — getAdapter(terminalProgram: string | null): TerminalAdapter. Looks up by name (Ghostty → ghostty adapter), falls back to generic for unknown values.

No callers yet — pure addition. Verify: bun --hot loads the modules without errors; importing getAdapter(null) returns generic; importing getAdapter('Ghostty') returns ghostty.
notes:
(Adds to existing notes — DO NOT replace conventions section, augment it)

BRANCH SETUP — this is the FIRST task; it creates the branch.
  git checkout main && git pull
  git checkout -b terminal-title-summary

TESTS to add in this task (co-located *.test.ts):
- shared/terminals/format.test.ts
    * formatTitle(peer) produces '[<id>] <summary>'
    * truncates to MAX_TITLE_LEN
    * strips control bytes (\x00-\x1f, \x7f) from summary
    * falls back to '[<id>] <runtime>' when summary is empty
    * preserves Unicode in summary
- shared/terminals/index.test.ts
    * getAdapter('Ghostty') returns the ghostty adapter (check by name)
    * getAdapter(null) returns the generic adapter
    * getAdapter('iTerm.app') returns generic (unknown → fallback)
    * getAdapter('') returns generic
- shared/terminals/generic.test.ts
    * Extract a small pure helper buildTitleBytes(title): Uint8Array (or string) from generic.ts so the wire format is testable
    * Assert it produces ESC + ']2;' + sanitized + BEL exactly
    * Assert clearTitleBytes() produces ESC + ']2;' + BEL with empty payload

Run: bun test — all should pass before closing this task.

HUMAN VERIFICATION
- bun test runs cleanly with no flakes.
- ls shared/terminals/ shows the 5 expected files (types, generic, ghostty, format, index) plus their .test.ts siblings.

title: Add flash_terminal MCP tool to highlight terminal window
description:
Followup from the set_summary→terminal-title work. Add an MCP tool an agent can call to draw user attention to its hosting terminal window — useful when paused on a question, finished a long task, or blocked.

Mechanism: write to the peer's TTY device (already stored on the peer row, captured at registration in runtimes/claude/server.ts:113). Three options for what to write:
- BEL (0x07): Ghostty bounces dock icon once, adds 🔔 to title. Quiet.
- OSC 9 (\033]9;<msg>\007): macOS notification banner via Ghostty.
- Both: banner + bounce.

Likely shape: tool takes optional level (subtle|normal|silent) and message; broker exposes POST /flash-terminal {id, message?, level?} that calls a shared helper alongside the title-write helper from the parent feature.

Open question deferred from initial discussion: which default behavior. User wanted to defer until usage patterns are clearer.
